title: Test Point Insertion with ATPG-Free Self-Supervised Learning
evidence_span: The ATPG-free TPI pipeline trains an autoencoder on bit sequences, propagates embeddings through reconvergent regions, infers controllability from embeddings, and estimates observability with saliency maps; the description claims effective insertion without ATPG labels or reinforcement-learning overhead.
problem: Test-point insertion is NP-hard, conventional testability metrics fail on reconvergent fanout, and supervised or RL approaches require costly labels or unstable runtime.
method_or_artifact: Self-supervised autoencoder and propagation model for embedding-based controllability and saliency-based observability estimation.
workload_or_benchmark: Digital test-point insertion circuits with reconvergent fanout; pattern-count reduction, circuit suite, area/timing overhead, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: RTL/gate-level testability and scan-test flow; ATPG tool, fault model, technology library, and insertion constraints are unspecified.
limits: The description omits pattern-count, fault-coverage, area/timing, training cost, and generalization results.
Embedding-derived testability may fail on unseen circuit structures or fault distributions.
Official description only; DFT claims require paper-level fault and implementation verification.

title: Chipmodeler: LLM-Aided Reference Model Design for Agile Hardware Verification
evidence_span: ChipModeler uses design standardization, hierarchical agile modeling, and building-block generation to automate reference-model creation; evaluation on 300 diverse designs reports up to 58.99% performance improvement, 9.18x generation capacity, and 7.11x faster design/validation cycles versus manual methods.
problem: Reference-model development for functional IC verification becomes a major bottleneck as designs grow more complex and requires repeated expert effort.
method_or_artifact: LLM-assisted hierarchical reference-model generation with standardized design representations and reusable building blocks.
workload_or_benchmark: 300 diverse hardware designs compared with manual reference-model development; design languages, model correctness criteria, hardware platforms, and human baseline process are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Functional hardware-verification flow with LLM generation and validation; RTL complexity, simulator, model checker, and compute environment are unspecified.
metrics: 7.11x acceleration of design and validation cycles
limits: The description omits functional-equivalence rate, defect escape rate, human correction effort, prompt/model versions, and design distribution.
Generation speed does not establish verification adequacy or correctness without independent oracle checks.
Official description only; LLM verification claims require artifact and failure-case review.

title: Uvmarvel: an Automated LLM-Aided UVM Machine for Subsystem-Level RTL Verification
evidence_span: UVMarvel converts heterogeneous specifications into protocol-correct subsystem UVM testbenches using an intermediate representation and bus-protocol library, then uses signal tracking and Verilog patching for stimulus refinement; the description reports 95.65% average code coverage and 4.5-hour automated execution instead of several human working days.
problem: Subsystem-level UVM testbench construction and stimulus generation require extensive manual coding, repeated EDA runs, and protocol expertise.
method_or_artifact: LLM-aided UVM generation using an intermediate representation, bus-protocol library, signal tracker, and Verilog patching loop.
workload_or_benchmark: Subsystem RTL across mainstream bus protocols; designs, coverage methodology, functional coverage, simulator/tool versions, and manual baseline effort are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: RTL/UVM verification environment with protocol specifications and EDA simulation; target subsystems, testbench scale, and compute resources are unspecified.
baselines: manual UVM testbench construction and stimulus refinement
metrics: Several human working days for comparable manual effort
limits: Code coverage is not functional coverage or bug detection; the description omits escaped defects, coverage closure, and generated-test quality.
Execution time depends on design size, simulator/license resources, and human review assumptions.
Official description only; verification claims require reproducible benchmark and oracle analysis.

title: Train Once, Calibrate Always: Machine-Learning-Assisted Blind Calibration for Analog-to-Digital Converters
evidence_span: ConvRec and ResConv models perform input- and error-agnostic ADC calibration on 65-nm time-interleaved band-pass delta-sigma and 28-nm Nyquist SAR test chips; the description reports more than 20 dB SNDR and SFDR improvement without prior circuit, error-mechanism, or input-statistics knowledge.
problem: Existing ADC calibration requires known error mechanisms or input statistics, limiting correction of unforeseen static and dynamic errors.
method_or_artifact: Hybrid convolutional-recurrent and residual convolutional blind calibration models with accuracy-versus-hardware-cost tradeoffs.
workload_or_benchmark: Measured 65-nm TI-BPADC and 28-nm SAR ADC test chips; sampling conditions, error injections, model size, calibration latency, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Analog-to-digital converter test chips in 65-nm and 28-nm processes with ML calibration hardware/software; power, memory, throughput, and integration details are unspecified.
baselines: prior ML calibration requiring input statistics
limits: The description omits absolute SNDR/SFDR, area, power, latency, convergence data, and test-chip operating conditions.
Input/error agnosticism may depend on training distribution and measurement coverage; unforeseen errors are not automatically guaranteed to be corrected.
Official description only; silicon calibration claims require paper-level measurement and generalization checks.

title: Raise the Shields: A Modular RISC-V Extension for Post Quantum Cryptography
evidence_span: The open RISC-V PQC extension exposes scalar CV-X-IF instructions and a modular PQ-ALU for Keccak, sampling, modular/polynomial arithmetic, finite-field operations, and compression across ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and HQC; post-synthesis 65-nm ASIC characterization reports instruction cycles, power/energy estimates, and approximately 48 kGE area.
problem: Post-quantum schemes have diverse dominant kernels, making fixed accelerators difficult to reuse while constrained RISC-V systems need practical crypto agility.
method_or_artifact: Unified modular RISC-V extension and PQ-ALU spanning hash-, lattice-, and code-based cryptographic kernels, with open hardware/software stack.
workload_or_benchmark: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and HQC standardized algorithms plus candidates under evaluation; cycle, power, energy, and area methodology details are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: RISC-V core with CV-X-IF and modular PQ-ALU synthesized in 65-nm CMOS; core configuration, clock, memory, compiler, and post-layout conditions are unspecified.
metrics: Power and energy estimates per custom operation
limits: The description omits absolute throughput, energy, security validation, area breakdown, timing, and comparison conditions.
A unified extension may trade peak scheme-specific performance for reuse and software compatibility.
Official description only; ASIC and cryptographic claims require paper-level and artifact verification.
